results.prompt: Write a list of exactly 4 bullet points explaining why pipeline bubbles occur during single-stream inference.
results.response:
* Pipeline bubbles in single-stream inference occur due to data dependencies and operation latencies.
* If one operation in the pipeline has to wait for the result from a previous operation, it creates a bubble or idle time in the pipeline.
* Bubbles can also occur when the data rate does not match the processing rate, causing the pipeline to stall until the next data element is available.
* In single-stream inference, bubbles can reduce the overall throughput and efficiency of the pipeline, leading to wasted cycles and longer processing times.
